title: Four Seasons Hotel Lobby — Bespoke Metalwork & Display Furniture: From Inquiry to Acceptance
excerpt: How Guoyao Metalwork delivered the bespoke metalwork and display furniture for a Four Seasons-standard luxury hotel lobby — illuminated brass display vitrines, hammered brass consoles, marble-top service stations, a green lacquer back-bar wall and loose furniture — 18 documented stages from inquiry to acceptance, with 33 project photographs.
category: Hospitality · Hotel lobby FF&E metalwork + display joinery
coverImageAlt: A pair of illuminated hammered brass display vitrines glowing warm white in the factory, staged side by side for a matched-brightness check

images.alt: The kickoff meeting.
Site survey inside the lobby under fit-out.
Design development.
The sealed sample set: hammered brass plates, the approved green lacquer panel, fluted glass and the backlit sample box glowing at true density — the contractual finish reference for every unit in…
A finished brass vitrine powered up in the workshop — the warm cove washing the display deck evenly, no LED points, no edge leakage.
Console-height vitrine with its clear glass top set into the brass frame; the hammered texture catches the glow along every edge.
Two vitrines staged together for a matched-brightness check — the lobby will read them side by side, so the workshop balances them side by side.
The corner of a hammered brass console: two hand-worked faces meeting in one continuous texture — the detail the designer examined longest at sample stage.
Console frame tacked square on the bench.
Legs and rails coming together — hammered faces already finished, protected during assembly so the texture arrives in the lobby as it left the bench.
The glass shelf sliding into its channel: clear glass, straight setting, edges dressed so nothing scratches the brass it sits in.
A finished console with its glass top set — the silhouette the lobby will read: slim brass frame, hammered faces, one clean plane of glass.
The long marble-top console dry-fitted in the workshop: stone templated against the actual brass frame, not a nominal dimension.
Counter with its woven brass mesh shelf below — service function dressed as joinery, standing on protective blocks awaiting top polishing.
The housekeeping service station: brass frame, marble top, green lacquered doors with brass RECYCLING and RUBBISH lettering, woven panel flat and true.
A back-bar module fresh through its lacquer sequence — deep green, edges trimmed in brass, shelves set square before hardware goes on.
Brass trim detail at a module edge: the two materials meeting with a hairline reveal, checked against the sealed sample under raking light.
The full back-bar wall stood and squared in the workshop — numbered modules trial-assembled so the lobby install is a repeat, not a rehearsal.
The central counter beam set into the wall composition, brass face to the room, lacquer reveals even across the junction.
The low cabinet run completing the wall — doors aligned to the same reveal standard as the service stations.
The side-table pair: turned lacquered legs in green and rose under stone and timber tops — proportion checked against the approved profile before packing.
A leg turning in close view: the lacquer depth even, the shoulder where turning meets top machined clean.
The vitrine family lit together for tuning — evenness checked from the guest distance, unit by unit, and logged.
A case photographed at full warmth in a darkened corner of the workshop: the register the lobby will carry after dark.
Close-up of the lit edge — hammered brass catching the cove glow, diffuser doing its work, no visible source.
Final inspection under the work lamp: a vitrine checked item by item against the QC sheet — glow, glass, frame tone — before it may be packed.
A wrapped console entering its plywood crate — foam, edge protectors and desiccant in place, crate labelled to the installation sequence.
Container loading at the factory: crates guided up the ramp onto a padded deck, blocked and strapped to the loading plan before sealing.
Positioning a vitrine in the lobby: white gloves, felt sliders, protection down — the sequence rehearsed in the workshop, repeated on site.
Leveling a console at the stone joint: shims set, spirit level centred — the invisible pass that makes the furniture read as built-in.
Evening commissioning: the vitrine glow checked against the workshop baseline while the back-bar wall reads depth under warm light.
The acceptance walk: hotel projects manager and our project lead through the finished lobby with the punch list, against the sealed samples and the commissioning log.
Aftercare in practice: brass polished to the approved tone on the first scheduled service visit — the maintenance the furniture was designed to receive.
